title: Private upgrade telemetry: dashboard + alert notes (draft)
content:
Context
- This is for the “Private upgrade + rollback mechanism” project (VPC + on-prem).
- Goal: have an operator + SRE-friendly view of every upgrade run, plus sane alerting that doesn’t page us for expected maintenance-window noise.
- Inputs:
  - Installer emits structured logs + diagnostics tarball (PR 444).
  - Observability pack adds dashboards + alerts (PR 311).
  - Control plane propagates “upgrade correlation id” across services (PR 18544) — not directly in scope here but impacts how we stitch traces/logs.

Non-goals (for telemetry v1)
- Not building a full workflow UI. Dashboards should be enough for GA.
- Not defining customer-facing dashboards (these are internal SRE + Support). Customer-facing can come later via Console.

Key questions to answer quickly during an upgrade
1) Is there an upgrade running right now? For which customer / cluster? What version -> version?
2) What step is it stuck on? Is it progressing?
3) Is the control plane still healthy? Did gateways go degraded? Are runtimes serving?
4) Do we need rollback? If yes, is rollback allowed (forward-only migrations)?
5) If it failed, where is the diagnostics bundle and what’s inside it?

Proposed dashboard set
A) “Private Upgrades Overview” (landing)
- Top tiles:
  - Upgrades in progress (count)
  - Upgrades failed in last 24h (count)
  - Rollbacks triggered in last 24h (count)
  - Median upgrade duration (7d) + p95
- Table: latest N runs
  - customer_id / deployment_id
  - env_type: vpc | onprem
  - from_version -> to_version
  - status: running | succeeded | failed | rolled_back | aborted
  - current_step_name + step_elapsed
  - correlation_id (click-through)
  - diagnostics_bundle_uri (if failed)
- Time series:
  - run failure rate (%) by version pair (to catch “bad release” patterns)
  - step duration p95 by step_name (spot regressions)

B) “Upgrade run detail” (drill-down by correlation_id)
- Event stream (ordered): prechecks -> backup -> upgrade steps -> postchecks
- Gantt-like visualization:
  - each step start/end + outcome + retries
  - show total wall-clock vs step time
- Inline health panels during the run:
  - control plane API error rate
  - gateway readiness / rollout status
  - runtime serving error rate
  - DB migration status (if we can surface it)
- Links:
  - installer logs (if centralized)
  - k8s events (namespaces filtered)
  - diagnostics bundle download

C) “Upgrade step health (fleet)”
- For each step_name:
  - success rate 7d
  - p50/p95 duration
  - top failure reasons (needs consistent reason codes)
- Useful for Release Eng to see “which step breaks most often” (e.g., backup verification / image pull / schema gate).

D) “Rollback runs”
- Similar to run detail but specifically:
  - reason rollback triggered (auto vs operator)
  - rollback allowed check result (blocked vs allowed) and why
  - snapshot restore duration
  - post-rollback service health confirmation

Metric naming and cardinality notes
We need to be careful on labels. We want high-level slicing without blowing up cardinality (esp. customer_id).

Strong preference: metrics are emitted by the installer/upgrade controller with a small set of labels, and detailed per-customer info stays in logs/events.

Candidate metrics (Prometheus style naming)
1) Upgrade run lifecycle
- redwood_private_upgrade_runs_total{result="succeeded|failed|aborted|rolled_back", env_type="vpc|onprem"}
- redwood_private_upgrade_run_duration_seconds{result=..., env_type=...} (histogram)
- redwood_private_upgrade_in_progress{env_type=...} (gauge)

2) Step-level telemetry
- redwood_private_upgrade_step_duration_seconds{step_name="prechecks|backup|apply_control_plane|apply_gateway|smoke_test|...", result="succeeded|failed|skipped", env_type="vpc|onprem"} (histogram)
- redwood_private_upgrade_step_retries_total{step_name=..., env_type=...}
- redwood_private_upgrade_step_failures_total{step_name=..., reason_code="disk_space|k8s_version|auth|schema_guard|image_pull|timeout|unknown", env_type=...}

3) Backup/restore specifics
- redwood_private_upgrade_backup_duration_seconds{backup_type="db_snapshot|config_backup|pv_snapshot", result=..., env_type=...}
- redwood_private_upgrade_backup_verify_total{backup_type=..., result=...}
- redwood_private_upgrade_restore_duration_seconds{restore_type="db_snapshot|config_backup|pv_snapshot", result=..., env_type=...}

4) Precheck outcomes (don’t over-label)
- redwood_private_upgrade_precheck_failures_total{check_name="k8s_version|disk_space|permissions|storage_class|secrets", severity="hard|soft", env_type=...}

5) Correlation id propagation / stitching
- Avoid adding correlation_id as a metric label.
- correlation_id should be in structured logs and trace attributes; dashboards can have a variable where you paste the correlation id to filter logs.

Label guidance (to reduce noise + cardinality)
- OK labels:
  - env_type (vpc/onprem)
  - result (succ/fail)
  - step_name (bounded list)
  - reason_code (bounded list)
  - from_major / to_major (optional; careful)
- Avoid labels:
  - customer_id, deployment_id, cluster_name
  - exact from_version/to_version if we have many patch versions (maybe aggregate by minor).

Log/event schema (for drill-down)
We should align reason codes and step names between:
- installer structured logs
- metrics reason_code/step_name
- diagnostics bundle summary.json

Minimum fields for each upgrade event log line:
- timestamp
- correlation_id
- deployment_id (or internal id)
- step_name
- step_state: started|progress|completed
- result: succeeded|failed|skipped
- reason_code (if failed)
- remediation_hint (short)
- artifact pointers (diagnostics_bundle_uri, snapshot_id)

Alerting proposal (v1)
Principle: maintenance windows exist; we shouldn’t page for “upgrade failed” unless it affects service availability beyond expected maintenance OR signals systemic release issue.

Pager vs ticket vs dashboard-only
PAGER (SRE on-call)
1) “Upgrade left deployment unhealthy after completion/abort”
- Trigger if upgrade run ends (failed/aborted/rolled_back) AND postcheck indicates control plane/gateway/runtime health below threshold for > X minutes.
- This is the real user impact.
- Data source: postcheck metric + service health SLO signals.

2) “Upgrade controller stuck (no progress)”
- If redwood_private_upgrade_in_progress == 1 and no step transition for > 20m (tunable) AND not in known long-running step (backup/pv_snapshot).
- Concern: deadlock; operator may be blocked; could exceed maintenance window.

TICKET (Support/Release Eng triage)
3) “Upgrade failure rate spike for a version pair”
- Failure rate > N% in last 6h AND runs_total >= minimum sample size.
- Route to Release Eng (Connor) + PM (Vivek) + SRE FYI.

4) “Step duration regression”
- p95 step duration increases > 2x vs 7d baseline for step_name (especially backup verification, schema gate, gateway rollout).
- Ticket with dashboards link; no pager.

DASHBOARD-ONLY
5) Precheck failures (expected)
- Operators will run prechecks multiple times; lots of soft failures expected.
- Don’t alert; instead provide a “Top precheck failures” panel.

Noise concerns / mitigation
- Prechecks:
  - Avoid alerting on precheck failures; expected during readiness.
  - Ensure severity is emitted (hard vs soft) and remediation_hint is useful.
- Backup duration:
  - Backup durations are workload-dependent; step regression alerts should compare against baseline per env_type and (maybe) storage class type, but we probably can’t label storage class (cardinality). For v1, compare only to global baseline and keep it ticket-level.
- Upgrade success rate:
  - Low volume environments will flap. Use minimum run count before firing.
- “In progress” gauges:
  - Risk: stale gauge on crash. Prefer heartbeat metric: redwood_private_upgrade_controller_heartbeat_seconds{env_type=...} + alert on absence.

Suggested thresholds (initial; revisit after beta)
- Stuck/no-progress: 20m (except backup/pv_snapshot steps where we allow up to 60m before warning).
- Post-upgrade unhealthy: 10m sustained errors after run end (pager).
- Failure rate spike: > 30% failures AND at least 5 runs in 6h (ticket).
- Step duration regression: p95 > 2x 7d p95 AND at least 10 observations (ticket).

Dashboards: panels to include (quick list)
Landing:
- Runs total by result (stacked)
- Run duration p50/p95 by env_type
- Failures by reason_code (top 10)
- Step failures by step_name (heatmap)
- Rollback triggers total

Run detail:
- Step Gantt table (from logs or from step_duration histogram + step start events)
- “Current step logs” (filtered by correlation_id)
- “Kubernetes events” (namespace filter: redwood-system, redwood-gateway, redwood-runtime)
- Health: control plane 5xx rate, gateway ready replicas, runtime error rate

Implementation notes / dependencies
- We need stable, bounded step_name list. Action: define in installer as constants and document.
- reason_code taxonomy needs to be agreed with installer + Support. Action: Allison + Jacob to review for Support readability.
- diagnostics_bundle_uri should be surfaced in logs and (optionally) as an annotation in the run summary event.
- For on-prem air-gapped: metrics export path might differ; make sure dashboards work when metrics are scraped locally and then forwarded (or not forwarded). At least ensure dashboards degrade gracefully (show “no data”).

Open questions
1) Where do we store the “upgrade run summary”? (control plane DB vs installer local). For dashboards, we’re assuming metrics/logs exist centrally.
2) Do we want a single ‘upgrade_run_id’ separate from correlation_id? (correlation_id currently the stitching key.)
3) How do we tag “customer-initiated maintenance window” vs “unexpected”? Might help alert routing.
4) Can we emit a synthetic “postcheck pass/fail” metric so the “unhealthy after run” pager is reliable?
5) On-prem: if customers don’t allow outbound telemetry, do we still ship a local Grafana dashboard bundle? (Probably PS-owned; note for Markus.)

Action items
- [Aisha] Propose final metric names + label set to installer team (Devon) and observability pack (Allison). Target: align before next beta rehearsal.
- [Sean] Define pager policy: when upgrade failures become on-call events vs support-only.
- [Jacob] Confirm diagnostics bundle contents include: precheck report JSON, step timings, k8s events, last N lines for key pods.
- [Connor] Confirm we can detect “no step progress” deterministically from emitted events.

Notes to self
- Keep dashboards oriented around “run” and “step” first; don’t overload with general CP metrics. Link to existing CP dashboards.
- Avoid anything that requires customer_id in Prom labels; we can still filter logs by deployment_id/correlation_id.
